To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) DCs are activated by apoptotic activated CD4+T cells (ApoACT) and (ii) DCs exposed to apoptotic uninfacted CD4+Tcells (ApoACT or ApoINF) secreted MIP1α, Mip1β, MCP1, and TNFa; this effect was not abrogated by the presence of HIV.
exposure of dendritic cells to activated CD4+ apoptotic T cells induces expression of APOBEG3G and maturation, and that these events are associated with reduced HIV infection of DCs.
exposure to apoptotic activated CD4+T cells induces maturation of human DCs and expression of APOBECT3G in these cells, which results in inhibition of HIV-1 infection in DCs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of apoptotic cells in the induction of maturation and activation of dendritic cells.
the mechanisms by which DCs are activated and matured by apoptotic activated CD4+T cells and how this process can be exploited to inhibit HIV-infection.
the role of APOB3G in DCs and its potential for inhibiting HIV-infection in this cell type.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ApoInf and ApoAct induce DC activation and maturation.
DCs can be infected by HIV-1 in vitro, however, in vivo, the infection of DCs by HIV-1 is very low.
the DCs are activated upon co-culture with apoptotic CD4+ T cell and that this activation is associated with the induction of APOBE3G in DCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
apoptotic activated CD4+T cells (Apo-Act) induce DC maturation and APOBECE3G-mediated inhibition of HIV-1 infection in DCs.
DCs are exposed to apoptotic activated CD4+T cells during HIV infection and that DCs respond to apoptotic activated cells by maturation and induction of APOBE3G.

the activation status of the apoptotic CD4+ T cell is a critical factor in the ability of DCs to respond to apoptotic CD4 T cells, and the ability to respond to ApoAct is critical for the ability of DC to inhibit HIV infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
exposure of DCs to apoptotic activated T cells results in a reduction in HIV infection in DC.
exposure of DC to ApoAct induces APOBEC expression, which in turn inhibits HIV infection in DC.
exposure of DCs to apoptotic activated CD4+T cells (Apo-Act) induces maturation and APOBECE3G-mediated inhibition of HIV infection in dendritic cells.
